data.title: DHL Group Lifts Guidance After Positive Earnings, Strong Peak-Season Forecast
data.description:
By Andrea Figueras 




  DHL Group upgraded its outlook for 2026 on the back of positive momentum and prospects of a strong seasonal peak in the last quarter of the year. 



  The German logistics company said Friday that it now expects earnings before interest and taxes to surpass 7 billion euros, or $7.86 billion, compared with a prior forecast of more than 6.5 billion euros. The group intends to review its midterm earnings guidance in March. 



  "Business development in the third quarter showed a broad-based growth in demand and, overall, positive earnings momentum for the group, particularly in the DHL Express division," it said. 



  According to preliminary figures, the group made EBIT of roughly 1.71 billion euros for the quarter through September, up around 16% compared with the same period a year earlier. Group revenue jumped more than 12% on year to nearly 22.6 billion euros. 



  The company also upgraded its target for free cash flow excluding net mergers and acquisitions to more than 3.2 billion euros, up from approximately 3 billion euros previously. 



  Capital expenditure is now estimated at around 3.6 billion euros from a prior range between 3 billion euros and 3.3 billion euros. 



  DHL plans to publish its third-quarter report on Nov. 5. 





  Write to Andrea Figueras at andrea.figueras@wsj.com

data.title: Trumpery Times Launches Satirical Humor Website Featuring Fictional Characters and Parody Stories
data.description:
SHERIDAN, WY / ACCESS Newswire / October 16, 2026 / Trumpery Times has launched as a satirical digital publication that uses parody, exaggeration and fiction to present fictional stories about entertainment, internet culture and popular media. The website is now live at https://trumperytimes.com and is publishing its initial collection of fictional stories and invented profiles.

The publication borrows the familiar language of online media, including headlines, interviews, profiles and feature stories, and uses it as the format for its humorous fiction. Each story begins with a recognizable cultural idea and then develops it into a fictional storyline. All characters, events and situations on the site are fictional and are presented as satire, not as factual reporting.

Coverage includes celebrity culture, film, popular culture and the media industry itself. The publication is written for readers who enjoy satire and parody related to entertainment and media. Familiar formats such as headline-driven stories, celebrity profiles and entertainment features serve as the framework, while the content inside them is invented.

"Satire relies on recognizable subject matter," said Lucas Komerlin, founder of Trumpery Times. "Readers need to recognize the starting point before the story moves into fiction. Trumpery Times starts with familiar subjects and develops them into fictional stories."

That approach shapes how every story on the site is built. A familiar idea provides the starting point, and exaggeration is used to develop the story. As the story develops, the connection to reality gradually loosens until the situation on the page is clearly invented. The goal is for readers to recognize where a story began while following how the story develops.

"Each story begins with a familiar idea and then develops into an invented situation," said Komerlin. "The challenge is deciding how far that idea can be extended while keeping a clear connection to what inspired it."

The publication's tagline, "Don't Believe Everything You Read," reflects the purpose of the publication. It signals that the site is built for entertainment and that its stories are not intended to be taken as news. Stories are written as clearly labeled fiction, and the familiar formats of media are used as a creative device, not as a way to mislead.

"The intention is not to disguise fiction as news, but to use the familiar language of news and popular media to create satire," said Komerlin.

Trumpery Times combines recognizable cultural references with fictional characters, invented situations and exaggerated narratives, organized around entertainment, film, popular culture and media-themed features.

Trumpery Times aims to give readers a space where familiar parts of contemporary culture appear in fictional and exaggerated forms. Visitors can browse the initial collection of satirical stories and fictional profiles through the website.

About Trumpery Times

Trumpery Times is a satirical digital publication covering entertainment, popular culture and modern media through parody, exaggeration and fictional storytelling. The publication presents familiar cultural ideas through fictional storylines and invented characters. Trumpery Times is operated by Raya Do Yaya LLC. Its guiding principle is simple: "Don't Believe Everything You Read." For more information, visit https://trumperytimes.com.

data.title: Diesel Prices Hold High Despite Efforts to Boost -2-
data.description:
0832 GMT - Oil prices above $100 a barrel look increasingly stretched relative to market fundamentals, says Norbert Rucker, head economics and next generation research at Julius Baer. Middle Eastern exports have largely recovered and global oil inventories remain comfortable. The Iran war has mainly erased the surplus accumulated in 2025 instead of pushing the market into a deficit. Diesel supply concerns could also ease as higher product exports and reduced refinery maintenance support availability, he says. The bank retains a cautious view on oil and a short position, saying geopolitical risk premiums and elevated freight rates may unwind. (jiahui.huang@wsj.com; @ivy_jiahuihuang)

--

Gold Rises on Softer U.S. Dollar -- Market Talk

0820 GMT - Gold prices rise on a softer U.S. dollar, with New York futures up 0.7% to $4,200.80 a troy ounce. "Hotter-than-expected consumer and producer inflation readings have failed to trigger renewed selling, with the rebound instead supported by falling bond yields, a softer dollar and a midweek wobble in equity markets, particularly technology stocks," analysts at Saxo Bank say. Key resistance remains around $4,235, a level breached during the late-September selloff. Meanwhile, Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh declined to signal whether the central bank will raise interest rates at its October meeting. According to the FedWatch tool, traders see a 15% chance of a rate hike this month and a 90% probability in December. (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)

--

TotalEnergies Unlikely to Deviate From Planned $2.5 Billion Buyback -- Market Talk

0817 GMT - TotalEnergies is unlikely to increase its quarterly share buyback above the $2.5 billion that it has already flagged, UBS analyst Henri Patricot writes after the company's third-quarter update. However, the French energy major's commentary suggests that there could be upside to the cash flow from operation guidance of $40 billion, he writes. UBS sees the company generating $42.5 billion. Shares fall 0.6% to 79.71 euros. (adam.whittaker@wsj.com)

--

Nestle's U.S. PetCare, Coffee Seen as Swing Factors in 3Q -- Market Talk

0741 GMT - Nestle's U.S. PetCare and coffee businesses are key swing factors in the upcoming third-quarter update, analysts at Barclays say in a note. Its PetCare business faced retailer destocking pressures in the second quarter, because customers had elevated inventories built up from when supply was constrained in the past, the analysts write. Coffee should also benefit as customers adjust to prior price rises, they say, particularly in the Starbucks platform. The consumer-foods giant's shares are up 0.9% at 81.80 Swiss francs. (aimee.look@wsj.com)

--

Comex Gold Futures Likely Consolidating, Chart Shows -- Market Talk

0724 GMT - Comex gold futures are likely consolidating, the daily chart suggests, RHB Retail Research's Aiman Kamil Bin Ahmad Shauqi says in a report. Gold could retest resistance at $4,200 per ounce if the current rebound continues, though the broader technical outlook remains bearish and resistance could prove difficult to break. Should bearish momentum continues in coming sessions, the precious metal could fall toward support at $4,000 per ounce. the analyst adds. Spot gold is 0.4% higher at $4,185.89 per ounce. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)

--

TotalEnergies' Debt to Fall Faster Than Expected -- Market Talk

0557 GMT - TotalEnergies could meet its below 10% gearing objective one quarter earlier than the end of 2026 target it set out at September's Investor Day, HSBC analyst Kim Fustier writes. Gearing is a way to measure a company's financial health and typically, the higher the gearing the less financially secure a company is. Quarterly cash flow from operations is set to benefit from an exceptional downstream performance and rebounding LNG prices. The French energy major's net debt should fall by around $7.0 billion on the prior quarter to $12.8 billion, she writes. This is almost $5 billion lower than HSBC's prior forecast and would push gearing down to 8.6% from 13.1% in the second quarter.(adam.whittaker@wsj.com)

--

TotalEnergies' Third-Quarter Update Pushes Expectations Higher -- Market Talk

0539 GMT - TotalEnergies' stronger-than-expected third-quarter update was driven by an exceptional downstream performance and rebounding LNG prices, HSBC analyst Kim Fustier writes. HSBC increases its quarterly earnings estimates by 34%, or $2.3 billion, to $9 billion--15% above Visible Alpha consensus. The largest revision was in the refining and chemicals unit, with an $1.5 billion increase to reflect the capture of higher margins and robust oil trading, she says. (adam.whittaker@wsj.com)

--

Iron Ore Edges Higher in Likely Technical Rebound -- Market Talk

0218 GMT - Iron ore prices are higher in early Asian trade in a likely technical rebound. Iron ore recently traded below US$90 a ton for the first time since 2024 as fundamentals continue to weaken, ANZ Research analysts say in a research note. Better investor sentiment across different assets and markets after a sharp selloff in the previous session likely provide some support. However, Chinese crude steel output remain low amid thin margins for steel mills. As a result, there is no incentive to rebuild inventories of the steel making raw material, the analysts say. The most actively traded January iron ore contract on the Dalian Commodity Exchange rises 0.3% to 674.0 yuan a ton. (sherry.qin@wsj.com)

--

Copper Falls as Expectation for Rate Hikes, Stronger Dollar Weigh -- Market Talk

0152 GMT - Copper prices are lower in early Asian trade. Rising expectations for interest-rate hikes, a relatively strong dollar and elevated U.S. Treasury yields are weighing on sentiment, say Baocheng Futures analysts in a note. However, tight concentrate supply and mounting smelting losses in China could support prices. Structurally tight inventories outside China also offer support, they say. Copper prices are likely to remain rangebound at elevated levels in the near term, with the dollar's direction, policy developments and the extent of China's seasonal demand recovery in focus, they say. (jiahui.huang@wsj.com; @ivy_jiahuihuang)

--

Oil Falls, Weighed by IEA's Crude, Diesel Release Announcement -- Market Talk

0029 GMT - Oil falls in early trade, weighed down by the International Energy Agency's announcement to release crude oil and diesel fuel. The IEA said Thursday that the volume of emergency oil stocks being released by member countries would exceed the 400 million barrels agreed upon in March. Members have pledged to expedite the remaining releases of around 100 million barrels, including over 20 million barrels of diesel, the IEA said. Front-month WTI crude oil futures are down 0.6% at $97.41 a barrel, while front-month Brent crude oil futures are 0.4% lower at $105.52 a barrel.

data.title: Diesel Prices Hold High Despite Efforts to Boost Global Supplies — Commodities Roundup
data.description:
MARKET MOVEMENTS:

--Brent crude oil is up 2.1% at $108.17 a barrel.

--European benchmark gas is up 0.8% at 88.21 euros a megawatt-hour.

--Copper futures are up 0.5% at $14,384.50 a metric ton.

--Gold futures are up 0.4% at $4,186.20 a troy ounce. 




  TOP STORY: 



  Diesel Prices Hold High Despite Efforts to Boost Global Supplies -- Analysis 



  Diesel prices remain stubbornly high as inventories sit near historically low levels, despite efforts to ease pressure on refined-fuel markets through emergency stock releases or the easing of restrictions on Russian exports. 



  Wholesale diesel benchmarks in the U.S. and Europe have more than doubled year to date. New York Harbor distillate crack spreads, a key measure of U.S. diesel refining margins, are holding above $100 a barrel, while ICE gasoil crack spreads, the European equivalent, have retreated from recent highs but remain elevated at $78.77 a barrel. 



  The problem isn't simply expensive crude, but a shortage of refined products. 





  OTHER STORIES: 



  See the States Where High Gas Prices Are Hurting the Most 



  Energy prices are up all over the U.S., but the surge is hitting some regions harder than others. And that impact could affect next month's midterm elections. 



  Rising fuel costs tied to the Iran war are the main driver of inflation, which rose to 3.7% in September. But the national average masks wide differences from state to state. In Wyoming, the typical household has spent an extra $975 on gasoline this year because of the Iran war, according to estimates from Brown University's Climate Solutions Lab. In Oregon, the additional burden was just $339. 



  -- 



  EverWind Outlines C$10B Nova Scotia AI Data Center, Wind-Power Portfolio Plan 



  Canadian clean-energy developer EverWind is planning to invest 10 billion Canadian dollars (US$7.05 billion) to build an artificial-intelligence data-center campus and power assets in Nova Scotia. 



  The planned investment is set to include over C$8 billion to drive development, construction, and financing for the Point Tupper campus, alongside C$2 billion to advance EverWind's Nova Scotia onshore wind portfolio. 



  -- 



  Oil Slips as Traders Weigh IEA Reserve Releases, Hormuz Risks -- Update 



  Oil prices fell Friday as traders weighed plans to accelerate emergency oil-stock releases against persistent Middle East supply risks and uncertainty over shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. 



  December Brent crude futures were a touch lower at $105.82, while December West Texas Intermediate futures dropped 0.8% to $95.75 a barrel. 



  -- 



  Gas Exporter Venture Global Wants to Get In on AI Power Boom 



  Natural-gas exporter Venture Global VG is joining the race to provide power to the artificial-intelligence boom, aiming to build gas-fired generation at its facilities to supply electricity to data centers. 



  Venture Global said it has entered into agreements with GE Vernova GEV and Baker Hughes Energy Services to procure equipment for on-site power plants, including turbines and transformers, which have been in high demand. The deals will allow Venture Global over time to make up to 10 gigawatts of computing capacity available at sites the company owns or controls. 



  -- 



  Ithaca Energy CEO Luciano Vasques to Step Down 



  Ithaca Energy said it has begun the search for a new chief executive officer after Luciano Vasques informed the board he plans to retire from the company by the end of March next year. 



  Vasques joined the U.K.-listed energy company, which was recently promoted to the FTSE 100 index, as CEO in October 2024. He previously led Eni's U.K. oil and gas business, which was combined with Ithaca's North Sea assets. 



  -- 



  U.S. Corn Export Sales Hit High End of Forecasts 



  Export sales of U.S. corn landed on the high side of analyst forecasts for the week ended Oct. 8, according to the latest report from the Department of Agriculture. 



  In its latest weekly export sales report published Friday, the USDA said that corn sales for delivery in the 2026-27 marketing year totaled 1.12 million metric tons. Soybean sales for 2026-27 totaled 574,900 tons, and wheat sales were 319,900 tons. 



  -- 



  Singapore Palm Oil Stocks Fall as City-State Grapples With Worst Haze in Over a Decade 



  Singapore has been smothered by the worst haze in over a decade, prompting the government to vow to identify the firms responsible for Indonesian forest fires causing the toxic fumes. That weighed on shares of several Singapore-listed palm oil companies Friday. 



  Air pollution in the city-state reached levels the government classified as "very unhealthy," as a toxic fog shrouded buildings and halted some outdoor activities. Singapore's government has rolled out measures to help the public deal with the haze, such as handing out masks, setting up shelters protected from the fumes, and closing some outdoor sporting facilities. 





  MARKET TALKS: 



  Higher Oil Prices Lift Purchasing Power in Canada for Some -- Market Talk 



  1024 ET - Elevated oil prices boosted Canada's purchasing power but the gains are uneven across the country, Royal Bank of Canada says. Real gross domestic income expanded 3.1% on-year in 2Q, nearly triple the pace of real GDP growth after a 46% surge in oil added about C$12 billion a quarter to export revenue. Royal Bank says oil producers and resource-rich provinces are capturing a disproportionate share of the initial windfall, while most households face higher costs without offsetting income gains. This complicates monetary policy, since the Bank of Canada controls only one interest rate for the entire country, Royal Bank adds. (robb.stewart@wsj.com; @RobbMStewart) 



  -- 



  Evidence of Chinese Buying Doesn't Lift Soybeans -- Market Talk 



  1019 ET - The USDA this week announced multiple export sales of U.S. soybeans to China, including a new flash sale of 558,000 tons announced today. An additional 236,000 tons of soybeans sold to "unknown destinations" were also reported. "Unknown destinations" is an alternative moniker that's often used for Chinese buyers, although not necessarily the case. But CBOT soybeans are lower, as China's return to buying U.S. soybeans was at least partially expected, says Joe Davis of Futures International in a note. "The recent demand therefore provides support but has not yet been sufficient to offset harvest pressure." Soybeans fall 0.7%, while corn is off 0.7% and wheat slides 1.2%. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com) 



  -- 



  Crude Futures Steady As Conflicts Keep Sellers At Bay -- Market Talk 



  1001 ET - Oil futures are steady in early U.S. trading with continuing strikes in the Middle East, and the absence of a Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire keeping prices afloat while traders consider the IEA's plan to accelerate the release of 100 million barrels of emergency stocks, part of previously agreed supply. Unrest in the Middle East is the main driver and traders maintain a "buy the price breaks type trade," Dennis Kissler of BOK Financial says in a note. Front-month WTI is up 0.2% at $98.18 a barrel, and Brent is up 0.1% at $106.02 a barrel. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com) 



  -- 



  Cattle Climbs Even as Cutout Prices Sink -- Market Talk 



  0959 ET - Live cattle futures on the CME are up 0.2% to nearly $2.28 a pound. Firm trade is expected today, says AgResource in a note--and that's even though boxed beef prices were lower overnight. "The choice cutout value gave back much of its early-week gains," says the firm, adding that select cutouts also turned negative for the week yesterday. Cattle futures are back to their highest level since early August, with further gains potentially signaling a bigger rally, says AgResource. Lean hog futures are up 1%. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com) 



  -- 



  U.S. Natural Gas Futures Fall in Early Trading -- Market Talk 



  0910 ET - U.S. natural gas futures are sharply lower despite a cold snap in the Northeast that's likely to lift near-term heating demand, and rising LNG feedgas flows. "The selling started with Asian traders trimming back longs overnight but volumes have been somewhat limited so far, so this doesn't look like a move towards a bearish overall position," Gary Cunningham of Tradition Energy says in a note. "Supplies remain stable, up slightly from last week with the return of Gulf production, but we are seeing some reports of slightly lower flows in from Canada." Nymex natural gas is off 4.6% at $3.087/mmBtu.(anthony.harrup@wsj.com) 



  -- 



  Palm Oil Rises on Stronger Rival Edible Oils -- Market Talk 



  1019 GMT - Palm oil ended higher in Asian trading. Prices were likely supported by strength in rival edible oils and optimism over stronger early-October export demand, Kenanga Futures writes in a note. However, concerns about abundant tropical oil supply ahead of the weekend might have capped gains, it says. The Bursa Malaysia Derivatives contract for January delivery rose 44 ringgit to 4,769 ringgit a ton. (kimberley.kao@wsj.com) 



  -- 



  Oil Futures Ease But Remain on Track for Weekly Gains -- Market Talk 



  0835 GMT - Oil prices fall in early European trading but remain on track for weekly gains. Traders are weighing supply risks from continued attacks on shipping in the Middle East against the release of emergency oil reserves by the International Energy Agency. Brent crude falls 0.9% to $105 a barrel, while WTI declines 1% to $96.95 a barrel. For the week, Brent is up 0.3%, while WTI has gained 5.5%. "Uncertainty in the Middle East and concerns over the sustainability of oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz has the market pricing in a significant risk premium," according to ING. Meanwhile, the scale of the IEA's planned diesel release could disappoint the U.S., raising the prospect that the administration could again consider restricting diesel exports to bolster domestic supplies, analysts at the firm say. (giulia.petroni@wsj.com) 



  -- 



  Oil's $100 Rally May Be Short-Lived as Supply Concerns Ease -- Market Talk 



  (MORE TO FOLLOW) Dow Jones Newswires



  October 16, 2026 12:41 ET (16:41 GMT)

data.title: Sunwoda Digital Battery Passport Solution Among Finalists at 2026 edie Energy & Tech Awards
data.description:
Sunwoda Digital Battery Passport Solution Among Finalists at 2026 edie Energy & Tech Awards

Sunwoda Digital Battery Passport Solution Among Finalists at 2026 edie Energy & Tech Awards

PR Newswire

LONDON, Oct. 16, 2026

LONDON, Oct. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The 2026 edie Energy & Tech Awards ceremony took place in London today, with Wang Qiao, General Manager of Sunwoda Hungary, attending on behalf of the company. Sunwoda's Digital Battery Passport Solution was among the nine finalists in the Supply Chain & Scope 3 Decarbonisation Project of the Year category.

Organised by UK sustainability media platform edie, the category recognises value-chain decarbonisation through supplier engagement, procurement and improved data. Other finalists included Prologis and Mobilityways' Green Travel Programme, Syngenta's Collaborative Carbon Reduction and HH Global's Sustainable Procurement Framework. Sunwoda brought a battery lifecycle data solution to this cross-sector field.

The solution links battery value-chain data to support product carbon footprint management and sustainability disclosures. Battery data spanning raw material sourcing, manufacturing, use and recycling is dispersed among suppliers, manufacturers and downstream partners, complicating carbon accounting and traceability. Sunwoda's solution links product identity, carbon footprint and compliance information in one digital record. This supports emissions hotspot identification, supply-chain coordination and product sustainability disclosure preparation.

Development began in 2023, with collaborative pilots in 2024 and the platform's launch in October 2025. Six modules cover supply chain management, traceability mapping, product carbon footprint, due diligence, passport management and operational management. Covering 78 indicators, the platform integrates material sourcing, environmental performance and compliance records, helping partners collect and access information about the same battery product. Secure data exchange and permission-based access support collaboration while protecting data.

The platform has progressed to practical applications. In 2024, two battery passport projects jointly developed by Sunwoda and its partners were selected for the Global Battery Alliance's Battery Passport pilot programme. According to edie's project profile, Sunwoda completed five pilots in 2025 and engaged 28 key suppliers in carbon management.

Sunwoda has collaborated on battery passport development and applications with well-known domestic and international companies, including TÜV Rheinland and Siemens China. These collaborations build experience linking battery information across organisations and stages of use.

From 18 February 2027, the EU Battery Regulation requires passports for electric vehicle batteries, light means of transport batteries and industrial batteries above 2 kWh placed on the EU market or put into service. Sunwoda plans to release phase two of its battery passport platform in mid-December 2026. Before implementation, platform development and collaborative applications will help customers prepare battery disclosures and connect supply chain information.

data.title: Nymex Overview: U.S. Crude Prices on Track to End Six-Day Streak of Increases — OPIS
data.description:
Crude-oil and refined product futures prices were falling, but most remained on track to post weekly gains.

The November West Texas Intermediate crude contract was down by 45cts to $97.52/bbl in light trade on Friday. The more-active December contract was down 88cts to $95.62/bbl. The front-month contract is currently nearly $6/bbl above last Friday's settlement.

December Brent crude was down by 18cts to $105.74/bbl while January prices were flat at $103.17/bbl. December prices are $1/bbl ahead for the week.

ULSD futures were on track for a second day of declines, with the November contract falling by 5.6cts to $4.7896/gal, still about 5cts ahead of last week's settlement. The more-active December contract was down by 4.37cts to $4.6108/gal.

Most activity in RBOB was also focused on the next-month contract, with November prices falling by 4.08cts to $3.1394/gal and December prices trading 2.7cts lower to $3.0528/gal. RBOB futures are on track to end the week about 15cts/gal lower than last Friday.

U.S. crude prices have seen a six-day streak of increases as supply concerns have supported the market. Friday's declines come even after the Energy Information Administration on Thursday reported a sharp 8.6 million-bbl drop in U.S. commercial crude inventories.

But those concerns are being mitigated by the announcement by the International Energy Agency that member countries have agreed to accelerate the release of 100 million bbls of crude oil and refined products that they had previously announced would be put into markets.

The release is expected to include about 20 million bbl of diesel.

The week's increase in diesel futures prices is being felt by consumers, with the average retail diesel price Friday of $6.3261/gal marking the fourth day of increases and an increase of about 5cts/gal from last Friday.

Gasoline prices around the country Friday averaged $4.3271/gal, about 6cts/gal lower than a week ago.

data.title: In HelloNation, Real Estate Expert Corey Bishop Examines Hidden Maintenance Costs in Older Homes in Western Massachusetts
data.description:
In HelloNation, Real Estate Expert Corey Bishop Examines Hidden Maintenance Costs in Older Homes in Western Massachusetts

In HelloNation, Real Estate Expert Corey Bishop Examines Hidden Maintenance Costs in Older Homes in Western Massachusetts

PR Newswire

ADAMS, Mass., Oct. 16, 2026

Buyers and Sellers of Older Properties in Berkshire County Should Understand Inspection Requirements, Aging Systems, and Local Building Rules Before Entering the Market.

ADAMS, Mass., Oct. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- What should buyers and sellers know before purchasing or listing an older home in western Massachusetts? A HelloNation article examines what buyers and sellers need to understand about older homes in western Massachusetts, covering the inspection process, aging infrastructure, renovation complexity, and local building requirements.

Western Massachusetts is home to some of the most architecturally distinctive properties in New England. Towns like Adams and communities throughout Berkshire County include homes built across many generations, a number of which have been carefully maintained for decades. Purchasing or listing older homes in western Massachusetts requires a different kind of preparation than buyers and sellers might expect with more recently constructed properties.

The inspection process is where that difference first becomes clear. Older homes have longer histories, and that history shows up in the systems and structures that hold them together. A HelloNation article explains that a thorough inspection for an older property often goes beyond a standard walkthrough to include the foundation, electrical panel, plumbing materials, chimney, and roof structure, and that hiring an inspector with specific experience in older New England homes can prevent costly surprises after closing.

Electrical systems are among the most commonly flagged items in older homes in this region. Properties built before the mid-twentieth century may contain wiring configurations that do not meet current standards, including knob-and-tube wiring in some of the oldest structures. The article notes that these conditions require evaluation by a licensed electrician and can affect insurance coverage or financing terms, and that sellers who understand this in advance can address electrical concerns before they create complications during negotiations.

Plumbing also deserves careful attention in older properties. Lead pipes and galvanized steel lines can degrade over time, and replacing them is a significant undertaking. The article advises buyers to ask about pipe materials and water heater age and to review the full plumbing history during the inspection phase to avoid unexpected costs after closing.

Heating systems are another important area of focus in older homes in western Massachusetts. Many properties rely on oil-fired boilers or furnaces that may have been in service for many years. Real estate experts point to heating system age and condition as a key factor that both buyers and sellers should be prepared to address directly during any transaction.

Septic systems are found throughout many of the rural and semi-rural properties in this region. Massachusetts law requires sellers to obtain a Title 5 inspection before a property can transfer, and buyers should review those findings carefully as part of their due diligence. The article explains that a failed or marginal inspection can affect both the timeline and the final terms of a transaction, making it important to understand the status of the septic system early in the process.

Renovation projects in older homes can also be more complex than they initially appear. Original plaster walls, period woodwork, and older window systems carry both aesthetic value and ongoing maintenance demands. The article notes that projects in older homes sometimes reveal issues behind walls or under floors that were not visible during the initial inspection, and that buyers planning significant updates should budget for contingencies before locking in final renovation numbers.

Some properties in Adams and surrounding Berkshire County communities may fall under historic district guidelines that govern exterior changes. Buyers with significant renovation plans should connect with local building authorities before finalizing a purchase to confirm that their plans align with local regulations and any applicable preservation standards.

Sellers also benefit from understanding these factors before going to market. A pre-listing inspection can surface issues before a buyer's inspector finds them, giving sellers time to address concerns or price accordingly. Real estate experts note that sellers who can document recent system updates, repair history, and Title 5 compliance tend to move through transactions with fewer delays, and that local professionals, including those at Bishop West Real Estate, can help sellers prepare that documentation before listing.

data.title: Scientology Mission of Shizuoka Marks First Anniversary at Foot of Mount Fuji
data.description:
SHIZUOKA, JP / ACCESS Newswire / October 16, 2026 / The Church of Scientology Mission of Shizuoka marks its first anniversary on October 25, 2026, completing one year of operation at its location on Road 75 in Shizuoka City, Japan. The anniversary is the Mission's first annual milestone since it opened as an Ideal Scientology Mission in October 2025.

Shizuoka City is the capital of Shizuoka Prefecture, located on Honshu, the main island of Japan, between the Pacific coast and the slopes of Mount Fuji. The Mission serves residents of the city and the surrounding region, and is one of the Church of Scientology's centers in Japan.

Over its first year, the Mission has operated as a center for the introductory services of the Scientology religion. These include Life Improvement Courses on everyday subjects such as marriage, parenting, personal motivation and goal setting; seminars on topics including personal efficiency and the fundamentals of Dianetics and Scientology; and auditing, the religion's form of spiritual counseling. The Mission also maintains a Public Information Display with multimedia presentations on the beliefs and practices of the Scientology religion and on the life of its Founder. The display is open to visitors.

Scientology Missions are local centers of the Scientology religion that deliver its basic and introductory services. An Ideal Mission is one equipped to provide the full range of those services under one roof. The Shizuoka Mission opened on October 25, 2025, following a dedication ceremony attended by parishioners and guests from across Japan and from overseas, including Taiwan and Australia. The one-year mark follows the Mission's first full annual cycle of courses, seminars and public access.

At the Mission's dedication, the Executive Director said: "This Mission represents more than a building. It's a new starting point." One year later, the Mission is in regular operation, with courses, seminars and the Public Information Display open to residents of Shizuoka and the surrounding region.

The Church of Scientology Mission of Shizuoka is located on Road 75 in Shizuoka City, Shizuoka Prefecture, Japan. More information about the Scientology religion is available at scientology.org.
